questions.q: What exactly is a Decision Engine?
questions.a: A Decision Engine is a runtime that evaluates session signals (intent, engagement, context) to select the single best action to take next — show a discount, recommend a product, trigger a campaign — all computed on-device without server round-trips.

questions.q: Does the Decision Engine replace my marketing platform?
questions.a: No. The Decision Engine handles the selection logic on-device, then hands off the decision to your existing platforms (Braze, Insider, mParticle, Segment) for execution. Think of it as the brain, not the execution layer.

questions.q: How does on-device processing ensure privacy?
questions.a: All session signals and model inference happen locally on the user's device. No raw behavioral data ever leaves the device. Only anonymous, aggregated metrics are sent to cloud services for reporting.
Decision inference runs in under 10 milliseconds on modern devices. The entire Score → Decide → Handoff pipeline completes before your next screen render.
You can install the SDK in under 10 lines of code and be running decisions within minutes. No backend changes required for the basic integration.

Models are trained across devices without centralizing data. Each device computes model updates locally, encrypts them with differential privacy, and sends only the encrypted gradients to the aggregation server. The global model improves without ever seeing raw data.
Native SDKs for Android and iOS. Web SDK for browser-based applications. React Native bridge for cross-platform apps. All SDKs share the same decision runtime core.
Yes. Enterprise plans include on-premise deployment of the cloud services (dashboard, aggregation server, analytics). The SDK always runs on-device regardless.

principles.title: Security Principles
principles.subtitle: Six principles that guide every engineering decision.

01.title: Data Minimization
01.desc: Collect only what the decision engine needs. Session signals are ephemeral and never persisted on servers.

02.title: Local-First
02.desc: All inference runs on-device. The cloud never sees raw behavioral data — only anonymous, aggregated metrics.

03.title: Encryption Everywhere
03.desc: TLS 1.3 for all transport. AES-256-GCM for data at rest. Federated model updates encrypted with per-device keys.

04.title: Consent by Design
04.desc: Granular opt-in controls built into the SDK. Users choose what signals to share. Revocation is immediate.

05.title: Regulatory Alignment
05.desc: KVKK VERBIS registered. GDPR compliant. CCPA ready. Regular third-party audits with published results.

06.title: No Persistent IDs
06.desc: The Decision Engine uses ephemeral session tokens. No device fingerprinting. No cross-site tracking. No permanent identifiers.

About.title: Why build a Decision Engine?
About.subtitle: Marketing automation is broken. Millions of campaigns fire blindly at users who never asked for them. We built Aurict to fix this — one decision at a time.

01.title: Decisions belong at the edge
01.desc: Every millisecond of server latency degrades the user experience. By making decisions on-device, we eliminate round-trips and deliver truly instant personalization.

02.title: Privacy is not negotiable
02.desc: Sending raw behavioral data to the cloud is a liability, not a feature. On-device inference means privacy is the default state, not an afterthought.

03.title: One decision per session
03.desc: Bombarding users with multiple campaigns is counterproductive. The Decision Engine selects the single best action per session, maximizing impact without overwhelming the user.

04.title: Models should improve collectively, privately
04.desc: Federated learning lets models learn from every device without seeing any raw data. The collective intelligence grows while individual privacy remains absolute.

05.title: Transparency builds trust
05.desc: Every decision is logged with SHAP attribution. Users and operators can see exactly why a particular action was chosen. No black boxes.

06.title: Auditable infrastructure
06.desc: Every decision is logged with its reasons and versions. Enterprise customers can review the decision runtime, the SDKs, and the aggregation server under a commercial agreement.

team.title: Built by a distributed team
team.subtitle: Engineers, researchers, and privacy advocates working on the future of on-device intelligence.

Changelog.title: What's new in Aurict
Changelog.subtitle: Every release, documented. Every change, explained.

entries.title: Federated Learning Pipeline GA
entries.body: The federated learning pipeline is now generally available on Scale and Enterprise plans. Models can now be trained across millions of devices without centralizing any raw data. Includes differential privacy guarantees with epsilon=2.0 by default and a new aggregation dashboard in the console.

entries.title: iOS SDK 1.6.3 — Memory regression on session scoring
entries.body: Fixed a memory regression in the iOS SDK where session scoring models were retaining buffers across sessions. Peak memory usage reduced by 40% on devices with 4GB RAM or less.

entries.title: Decision latency reduced to sub-8ms
entries.body: Optimized the decision inference graph with operator fusion. P95 decision latency dropped from 12ms to 7.8ms on benchmark devices. Android SDK binary size reduced by 15%.

entries.title: SHAP explainability dashboard
entries.body: New explainability tab in the console shows feature contributions for every decision. Operators can inspect individual session decisions with waterfall charts showing which signals drove the action selection.

entries.title: Web SDK — Safari 18 Private Browsing fix
entries.body: Resolved an issue where the Web SDK's IndexedDB persistence layer was blocked in Safari 18 Private Browsing mode. The SDK now gracefully falls back to in-memory storage with a console warning.

entries.title: Braze and Insider handoff providers
entries.body: Native handoff integrations for Braze and Insider are now available. Decisions made on-device can be dispatched directly to either platform without additional server-side logic. Includes campaign mapping and response-tracking support.

entries.title: Breaking: Decision API v2 migration
entries.body: The Decision API has been updated to v2. The old `decide()` function is deprecated and will be removed in v2.0.0. Migrate to `session.evaluate()` with the new campaign context object. Migration guide available in docs.

entries.title: React Native bridge initialization 3x faster
entries.body: Rewrote the React Native bridge initialization to use lazy module loading. Bridge setup time reduced from ~450ms to ~140ms on cold start. Native module now compiled ahead-of-time.
